heroHeadline: Six Days to Sindoor Anniversary: AJK Launches 'Solidarity With Pakistan Army Week' as India Completes Emergency Airstrip Drills
heroSubtitle: On May 1, 2026 — six days before the first anniversary of Operation Sindoor (May 7, 2025) — Azad Kashmir launched a ten-day 'Solidarity with Pakistan Army Week' (May 1–10) featuring flag-hoisting, rallies, and prayer gatherings across all AJK districts, timed to span the exact anniversary window and ending on the ceasefire anniversary (May 10). Simultaneously, India's IAF concluded an emergency airstrip exercise on the Purvanchal Expressway in UP, certifying the Su-30 MKI, Mirage-2000, and Jaguar for highway combat landings — a direct response to Pakistan's airbase-strike attempts during Sindoor. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh disclosed on April 30 that India stopped Sindoor 'voluntarily, on our own terms' and called Pakistan's nuclear threats during the operation a 'bluff.' Both sides are mobilizing competing narratives for the anniversary week: India emphasizing voluntary restraint and strategic dominance; Pakistan emphasizing army solidarity and defensive prowess. Bilateral standoff continues unchanged: airspace closed until May 24 (both sides reciprocal), Indus Waters Treaty suspended, all trade halted, IWT at UNSC. S-400 regiment 4 en route from Russia, arriving mid-May to close the last air defence coverage gaps along the western border. India's military spending now 5th globally at $92.1B (SIPRI 2025).
